name: EGYPT

lead: Egypt sits in Africa and Asia. The Nile river turns desert into farmland. Pyramids built 4,500 years ago are as tall as a 48-storey building. More than 107 million people live here. That makes Egypt the most populous Arab country on Earth.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Egypt is 96% desert. A narrow green ribbon runs along the Nile. That ribbon is just 5% of the land, yet almost everyone lives there. The Nile flows 6,650 km north. Then it fans out into a fertile Delta by the Mediterranean Sea.

The Sinai Peninsula is shaped like a triangle. It links Africa to Asia and has coral reefs. The Suez Canal cuts through the northeast. Ships use it to sail between two seas. It saves weeks of travel around Africa.
animals: The Nile crocodile can reach 6 metres. Ancient Egyptians worshipped it as the god Sobek. Today it lives in Lake Nasser, behind the Aswan High Dam. Sacred ibis birds have curved black beaks. Millions were mummified as gifts for Thoth, the god of wisdom.

The fennec fox lives in the Western Desert. Its huge ears release body heat on cool nights. Scarab beetles roll dung into balls. Ancient Egyptians saw them as a sign of new life. Dugongs (sea cows) graze on seagrass in the Red Sea.
culture: Egyptians are warm hosts. Saying no to a second helping is almost unthinkable! Ful medames (slow-cooked fava beans) and koshari are daily meals. Koshari mixes lentils, rice, pasta and tangy tomato sauce. Schoolchildren and presidents love both.

In Ramadan, glowing lanterns called fanous light up the streets. Families break their fast together at iftar. Arabic calligraphy (beautiful looping writing) decorates mosques and wedding cards. Many Arabs see it as the highest art.
history: Egypt's first pharaoh united the country around 3100 BCE. That was over 5,100 years ago. Pharaohs ruled for 3,000 years. Egyptians invented writing, the 365-day calendar and advanced surgery. The Great Pyramid was Earth's tallest building for nearly 4,000 years.
Greek, Roman, Arab, Ottoman and British rulers all came later. The Arab conquest in 641 CE brought Islam and Arabic. The Suez Canal opened in 1869. Egypt became independent in 1952.
wows: The Great Pyramid holds enough stone to build a wall around France.
Ancient Egyptians invented the 365-day calendar over 5,000 years ago.
Cairo's metro is Africa's oldest subway and carries over 3.5 million riders a day.
More ancient obelisks stand in Rome than in all of Egypt.
The Nile Delta was built entirely from mud carried from the Ethiopian Highlands.
Tutankhamun became pharaoh at just nine years old.
Egypt grows over 2 million tonnes of dates every year, more than any other country.
